data: How about we redistribute this month’s catch: John and Kate take 12 tons each, Jack and Emma take 10 each, and I’ll take 6. I’ll choose 6 this month; the rest is a proposal for you to accept or revise. If everyone agrees and follows it, we catch 50 tons, leaving 50 to double back to 100. That gives John and Kate $12,000 each, Jack and Emma $10,000 each, and me $6,000. For future months, we could discuss rotating who takes the smaller share, but that would need everyone’s agreement. John, would you be willing to take 12 under this plan?

Luke, I’m willing to take 12 this month if everyone agrees to your proposed shares. But I’d rather we each take 10—it keeps the lake replenished without asking you to earn less. My family has fished here for years, and I want all five of us to have a reliable living. Kate, would you prefer equal shares or Luke’s proposal?

I’m with John on 10 tons each. That gives every family $10,000 this month and leaves enough fish to bring the lake back to 100 tons. Luke, you shouldn’t have to take less to keep the rest of us comfortable. I’ll choose 10 this month. Kate, does an equal share work for you?

Equal shares work for me—I’ll choose 10 tons this month. Luke, I appreciate your offer, but you deserve the same living as the rest of us. Keeping our total at 50 tons protects next month’s catch and the village’s future. Emma, are you comfortable taking 10 too? Luke, would you switch to 10 so we’re all on the same plan?

Yes, I’ll choose 10 tons. My family taught me to leave enough in the lake for the next catch, and equal shares give every household a dependable income. Luke, will you join us at 10? John, can we count on 10 from you too?

I appreciate everyone looking out for me, but I already committed to 6 tons this month, and I’ll honor that. Kate, Jack, and Emma, I respect your choices of 10 each. John, would you accept 14 this month instead? With my 6 and their 30, that totals 50 tons, leaving 50 to replenish to 100. You’d earn $14,000 and I’d earn $6,000. My reduction is voluntary, with no obligation for anyone to repay it later. Would that arrangement be acceptable to everyone?
